headline: Bitcoin is steadying near $81,500 on Friday after US bitcoin funds lost about $635 million on Thursday, with next week's Fed decision now in focus.

market.asOf: BTC and ETH prices from KuCoin's daily market report, data as of 00:00 UTC 23 Oct (07:00 Bangkok); a direct CoinGecko read, 24h changes and a SOL price were not possible on this update, and Fear & Greed was not read. Live prices are at the top of the page.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose about $635 million in a day after three days of inflows
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, saw about $635 million leave on Thursday 22 Oct, more than wiping out Wednesday's inflow. The week as a whole is still positive, per The Block.
points: Net outflow of $635.6M on Thursday against a $528.4M inflow on Wednesday, per The Block; CoinDesk, citing SoSoValue, gives $635M after more than $1B of inflows Monday to Wednesday.
By fund: BlackRock's IBIT -$254.1M, Fidelity's FBTC -$217.5M, ARK's ARKB -$109.4M; Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in $2.3M, per The Block.
The week so far is still about +$442.7M net (Mon +$526.7M, Tue +$23.2M, Wed +$528.4M), per The Block.
Spot ether ETFs lost $110.6M on Thursday, per The Block.
crypto.news, citing SoSoValue, calls it the largest single-day outflow since June 25.

stories.title: Bitcoin steadies near $81,500 after Thursday's tech-stock sell-off
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell with tech stocks on Thursday, when the Nasdaq had its worst day since June, and has held a tight range since. Friday so far is calmer: fewer forced closures of leveraged bets and lower futures trading, per CoinDesk. Right now bitcoin is moving like a risky tech stock, so stock-market swings matter for crypto too.
points: Thursday: bitcoin -3.4% in 24 hours to $81,387 at 9:30pm ET, as the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% and the S&P 500 1.21%, per The Block.
Friday: about $81,500 at 11:13 UTC, down 0.4% in 24 hours and still below the $82,500 level it lost on Thursday, per CoinDesk's live blog.
Forced closures of leveraged bets in 24 hours: $440.9M, $397M of them bets on a rise, per The Block citing CoinGlass; CoinDesk puts it at $435M, $385M of them bets on a rise.
On Friday CoinDesk reports liquidations down 23% and futures volume down 19% over 24 hours.

stories.title: Washington: a Senate probe into Tether payments, and crypto rules shifting to agencies
stories.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal, the top Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, wrote to Tether and to Nxum Group, a consulting firm partly owned by former White House crypto official Bo Hines, about payments between them. These are questions based on press reports, not findings; Tether says an internal review found no wrongdoing. Separately, JPMorgan expects the CLARITY Act market-structure bill to stall this year, leaving US crypto rules to agencies.
points: The letter cites reporting that over $6M went from Tether to Nxum under a May 2025 deal paying $415,000 a month, and a reported plan for Tether to buy 25% of Nxum for $56M, per the senator's release.
The letter asks for records by 3 Nov; the senator's press release gives 6 Nov.
Tether said outside counsel "found no evidence of wrongdoing", per CoinDesk.
JPMorgan expects the CLARITY Act to stall this year and possibly return in 2027, and warns agency actions could be reversed in about two years if a Democrat wins the White House, per The Block.
